name: weeknight vegetarian ragu
instructions:
The one-pan weeknight ragu: fry everything, eat with noodles and parmesan.

=== INGREDIENTS ===

- olive oil
- onion
- garlic
- eggplant
- mushrooms (any)
- bell pepper
- canned tomatoes and/or canned FIRE-ROASTED tomatoes — WHOLE, NOT CRUSHED (and no tomato paste — see notes)
- vegan beef crumbles
- salt and black pepper

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. Just fry it all in a pan.
2. Eat it with any noodle and parmesan cheese. (I like it with spaghetti.)

ANY INGREDIENT CAN BASICALLY BE OMITTED — cook from what's in the fridge.
notes:
=== SOUNDS CRUDE, BUT IN SOME WAYS IT ISN'T ===

It sounds crude as a recipe, but in some ways it isn't: it's THE MOST NATURAL WAY TO USE SOY BEEF CRUMBLES, which can be hard to place. The crumbles want exactly this — a busy pan of vegetables and whole tomatoes to disappear into.

=== WHOLE TOMATOES — TOMATO PASTE IS CLASHING ===

You really want WHOLE tomatoes here (canned, regular or fire-roasted — not crushed). Tomato paste is CLASHING.

=== FLEXIBILITY IS THE POINT ===

Any ingredient can basically be omitted. Any noodle works — SPAGHETTI is my pick. Parmesan over the top.

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- [[bolognese]] / [[fire-roasted-meatballs]]: the real-deal ragus — long-simmered, protein-forward. This is the no-ceremony weeknight end of that family.
- [[ratatouille]]: the same vegetable crowd (eggplant/pepper/tomato), french and vegetable-first instead of crumble-and-noodle.
